issues.description: Lecture constructor parameter order is inconsistent between the UML in the problem statement and the implemented/reference constructor. The UML attributes (problem_statement.md lines 64-68) list attributes in the order: numberOfInscribedStudents, lectureName, numberOfLecturers, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfTutors. The problem text's attribute list (problem_statement.md line 17) and the reference solution constructor (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 13) both place lectureName first (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). The problem text also instructs students to make the constructor follow the UML order (problem_statement.md lines 20-21). This contradiction can confuse students about the expected constructor signature and lead to mismatches between student implementations and the reference/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the intended constructor parameter order explicit and consistent across artifacts. Options: (A) Update the UML attribute order in problem_statement.md (lines 64-68) to match the textual list and the reference constructor (lectureName first), and add an explicit constructor signature to the template that matches that order; or (B) change the reference solution and template constructor to follow the UML order (numberOfInscribedStudents first) and update the textual list and any instructions to match. Also update the problem text where it tells students to follow the UML (problem_statement.md lines 20-21) to state the exact constructor parameter order chosen. Ensure tests and any provided constructor signature in the template match the chosen order.
